newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: PHILIPPINE STOCKS - factors to watch - April 3.
newsitem.headline: PHILIPPINE STOCKS - factors to watch - April 3.

text.p: Following are views on the direction of Philippine stocks on Thursday and main factors likely to affect trading.
* Shares are expected to continue weaker due to the Dow's heavy loss and a lack of domestic news, Noel Reyes, research head at Anscor-Hagedorn Securities, said.
* Listing of Equitable Banking Corp will hog the limelight in today's session but may be soured by Wall Street's slump, says Manuel Goseco, economist at Dharmala Securities Phils.
* The Dow Jones closed 94.04 points lower at 6,517.01. PLDT's ADR shed $0-1/2 at $59-5/8.

* Manila Bulletin says the Telecommunications Users Group of the Philippines strongly opposes the higher rates proposed by PLDT under the metering system slated for implementation by the second half of the year.
* Cosmos Bottling Corp posted 101 million pesos in net income for the first quarter of this year, 146 percent higher than the 41 million pesos in the same period in 1996.
* The Energy Regulatory Board has approved the application of the Manila Electric Co to restructure power rates that will reward efficient users of electricity.
* Empire East Land Holdings Inc, the housing development arm of Megaworld Properties & Holdings Inc, denied market speculation that the company was facing difficulties.

* Philippine Times Journal quotes Urban Bank chairman Arsenio Bartolome as saying that take-over of Victorias Milling Co by its creditors is a "possibility" once the agreed 90-day debt moratorium ends on June 30 this year.

* Newspaper BusinessWorld says bank treasurers cautioned against any further decline in local interest rates which could narrow the gap with that of U.S. rates and thus prompt foreign funds to pull out. The paper adds that the Central Bank said interest rates may still continue to go down but with little possibility of inducing capital flight.
* On Thursday, the Philippine Stock Exchange composite index slid 9.58 points to 3,162.21.
* The peso closed lower at 26.37 to the dollar vs 26.367
* The Philippine interbank call loan average was unchanged at 9.9375 percent.
